mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate relative to the prior month signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that increase corporate cost pressures and reduce consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) and consumer credit demand is contracting (RSAFS declining), it signals a tightening monetary policy combined with weak consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window, or negative returns do not materialize when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 102.0), the supply chain is robust and corporate margins are stable, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in less than 50% of instances when INDPRO > 102.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS increasing month-over-month) signals a strengthening labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in less than 55% of instances when PAYEMS rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer credit demand (RSAFS) falls below 600,000 million dollars, it signals reduced consumer spending power and weak economic demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in less than 40% of instances when RSAFS < 600000, or Rank IC falls below 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is rising (UNRATE > 4.0%) and industrial production is contracting (INDPRO < 100.0), it signals a dual shock to the labor market and supply chain, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window, or negative returns do not materialize when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in less than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.
